messages.subject: subsetting large .wav files and saving to a new directory
messages.subject_clean: subsetting large .wav files and saving to a new directory
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am interested in taking portions (~5 minute) from larger recordings (30 minute to 120 minute) of .wav files and saving these subsetted files in a new directory. Unfortunately, I'm somewhat of a novice in R, an cannot come up with a suitable string of code to accomplish this. So I was hoping somewhere in this group might be able to assist!

#Will something along the lines of this cut the first five minutes of each file?
sound_files <- list.files(path = "my_path", pattern = ".wav", full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)
seq_along(sound_files)
lapply(sound_files, cutw(sound_files, channel = l, from = 0.0, to = 0.300))

#When I attempt this, I receive the error message argument "f" is missing, with no default.

#I am also interested in saving each of these 5 minute .wav files but cannot find a way to do so. Is there a way to do this using savewav?

messages.subject: Release of seewave 2.1.4
messages.body_plain:
Dear seewave users,

A new version of seewave (2.1.4) has been pushed to CRAN a few days ago.

Please see the changes listed below.

Enjoy,

Jerome

---

NEW FUNCTION
o songmeterdiag(): diagnostics of .wav files as generated by SongMeter devices.

OTHER CHANGES
o ACI(): a small bug in a condition fixed.

messages.subject_clean: [seewave] subsetting large .wav files and saving to a new directory
messages.body_plain:
f is the sampling frequency of the file, it should be embedded in the original wav, if not you must pass it as an argument to cutw()
the following (untested) code should cut the files and save them in the working directory, using fuction writeWave from package tuneR. Replace f with your sampling frequency.

sound_files <- list.files(path = "my_path", pattern = ".wav", full.names = TRUE, recursive = FALSE)

for( i in 1:length( sound_files)){
filename=tools::file_path_sans_ext(basename(as.character( sound_files[i]))) # takes the orginal filename without the extension
wavcut= cutw(sound_files[i], f,  channel = l, from = 0.0, to = 0.300)
tuneR::writeWave(object = wavcut, filename = paste0( filename,"-cut",".wav"  ))
}

messages.subject: blur ratio and excess attenuation
messages.body_plain:
Hi all

when working with signal degradation: has anyone used seewave to calculate "blur ratio" and "excess attenuation" (for instance as defined by Dabelsteen et al in this paper <https://orbit.dtu.dk/files/4414480/Pedersen.pdf>)?. The formulas are not totally clear in the paper, so I would like to know if someone has been able to translate/implement them into R.

cheers

Marcelo
